title: Absolute difference
starter:
%x  = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=0
%y  = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=1
%d  = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=2
# d[i] = |x[i] - y[i]|, with i32 wraparound
%vx = load %x
%vy = load %y
%m1 = expand -1 shape=[4]
%ny = mul %vy %m1
%df = add %vx %ny
%s  = store %d %df
%d1 = after %d %s
hints: The starter stores `x - y`, which is negative when `y` is bigger. You want the larger of `x - y` and `y - x`.
Build `y - x` the same way (multiply `x` by an expanded `-1` and add `y`), then take `max` of the two vectors.
i32 wraps: `|INT_MIN - 0|` is still `INT_MIN`, because `0 - INT_MIN` wraps back to `INT_MIN`. The tests expect that.
explain: `max(x - y, y - x)` is the absolute difference, computed elementwise on shape `(4,)`. With wraparound, a difference that overflows stays wrapped, so `INT_MIN - 0` and `0 - INT_MIN` are both `INT_MIN`, and the max of the two is `INT_MIN`.
